chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Abū al-Qāsim, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man intends to go to the privy while he is wearing a ring on which is the Name of Allah, Exalted is He. He said, “I do not like that.” He said: Then if it is the name of Muḥammad? He said, “There is no harm in it.”

So this does not contradict what we have said, because his statement عليه السلام, “There is no harm in it,” when the name of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله is on it, only permits it for one who enters the privy while that is with him; and he did not permit him to perform istinjāʾ while it is in his hand and he thereby directly handles najāsah. Then he said, may Allah, Exalted is He, support him: And siwāk is not permissible while a person is in the state of relieving himself until he finishes from it. This indicates that.

key_terms.اسْمُ اللَّهِ: the Divine Name inscribed on the ring
key_terms.السِّوَاكُ: tooth-cleaning stick or brushing the teeth
key_terms.الْخَلَاءَ: the privy or place of relieving oneself
key_terms.الْغَائِطِ: the state or act of defecation
key_terms.خَاتَمٌ: a ring worn on the hand
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permitted in this context
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِيَ: to perform istinjāʾ, cleansing oneself after relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to enter the privy or perform istinjāʾ while wearing a ring engraved with the Name of Allah or the name Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This report addresses etiquettes and rulings related to entering the privy while wearing a ring bearing sacred names. It indicates dislike for entering with the Name of Allah, Exalted is He, and permits the presence of the name Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله, while clarifying that one should not directly handle najāsah with such a ring in hand.
